clips.text: Diwali sale night, eight PM. Ravi's handmade jutti store runs on his own website. Last year it froze at the worst moment, and Ravi can't read a server dashboard.
Insidious watches his store. On a real surge, in about thirty seconds, its guardian fires an incident. Checkout is crawling at nearly eight seconds.
clips.captionText: Insidious watches his store. On a real surge, in about thirty seconds, its guardian fires an incident. Checkout is crawling at nearly 8 seconds.

clips.text: The console prices it: about five point three lakh rupees an hour at risk.
clips.captionText: The console prices it: ≈ ₹5,32,980 an hour at risk.

clips.text: NudgeBee's AI finds the root cause, and Claude writes a plan.
Ravi asks how the shop is doing, in Tamil. He can use whatever language he thinks in: Tamil, Hindi, Tanglish or English, by voice or text. Sarvam understands, and replies in kind.
Claude's plan arrives as a Tanglish voice note, with three buttons.
Pause extras and add servers for about eight rupees an hour, only pause extras, or do nothing. Ravi taps one.
clips.captionText: Pause extras and add servers for about ₹8 an hour, only pause extras, or do nothing. Ravi taps one.

clips.text: One tap. Flagsmith switches off the heavy extras. Kubernetes adds a server. The database pool doubles. Checkout drops to under half a second, as NudgeBee measured.
A second approved plan added a real AWS read replica, and Flagsmith moved reads onto it.
NudgeBee's own AI confirms it, independently.
So, four to eight rupees an hour protects about five lakh an hour, by the console's estimate. It pays for itself, and Ravi never opened a terminal.
clips.captionText: So, ₹4–8 an hour protects about ₹5 lakh an hour, by the console's estimate. It pays for itself, and Ravi never opened a terminal.

clips.text: Under the hood: thirteen Flagsmith flags, from load-shedding and the database pool to an AI kill switch.
clips.captionText: Under the hood: 13 Flagsmith flags, from load-shedding and the database pool to an AI kill switch.
